BYLAWS OF HARBORLIGHT LITERACY ALLIANCE, INC.
A North Carolina Nonprofit Corporation

Adopted by the Board of Directors on January 24, 2026

ARTICLE I — NAME, PURPOSES, AND OFFICES

Section 1.1. Name. The name of the corporation is Harborlight Literacy Alliance, Inc.

Section 1.2. Purposes. The corporation is organized exclusively for charitable and educational purposes within the meaning of Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, including advancing adult literacy in the coastal counties of North Carolina.

Section 1.3. Principal Office. The principal office of the corporation is located in New Hanover County, North Carolina. The corporation may have other offices as the Board of Directors determines.

ARTICLE II — MEMBERS

Section 2.1. No Members. The corporation has no members. All rights that would otherwise vest in members vest in the Board of Directors.

ARTICLE III — BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Section 3.1. General Powers. The affairs of the corporation are managed by its Board of Directors.

Section 3.2. Number and Term. The Board consists of not fewer than five (5) and not more than fifteen (15) directors. Each director serves a three-year term and may serve no more than three consecutive terms.

Section 3.3. Election. Directors are elected by a majority of the directors then in office at the annual meeting.

Section 3.4. Vacancies. A vacancy is filled by a majority of the directors then in office, though less than a quorum, and the director so chosen serves for the unexpired term.

Section 3.5. Removal. A director may be removed, with or without cause, by a two-thirds vote of the directors then in office.

Section 3.6. Regular and Special Meetings. The Board holds a regular meeting at least quarterly. A special meeting may be called by the Chair or by any three directors on not less than five days notice.

Section 3.7. Quorum and Voting. A majority of the directors then in office constitutes a quorum. The act of a majority of the directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present is the act of the Board.

Section 3.8. Action Without a Meeting. Action required or permitted to be taken at a Board meeting may be taken without a meeting if each director signs a written consent describing the action, and the consent is filed with the minutes.

Section 3.9. Compensation. Directors serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for reasonable expenses.

ARTICLE IV — OFFICERS

Section 4.1. Officers. The officers are a Chair, a Vice Chair, a Secretary, and a Treasurer, each elected annually by the Board.

Section 4.2. Duties. The Chair presides at meetings of the Board. The Secretary keeps the minutes and gives notice of meetings. The Treasurer has custody of the corporate funds and renders an account at each regular meeting.

ARTICLE V — COMMITTEES

Section 5.1. Executive Committee. The Board may designate an Executive Committee of three or more directors, which may act for the Board between meetings except that it may not amend these Bylaws, elect or remove a director or officer, or approve a dissolution or a sale of substantially all assets.

Section 5.2. Audit Committee. The Board maintains an Audit Committee of not fewer than three directors, none of whom is an officer or employee, which engages the independent accountant and reviews the annual financial statements.

ARTICLE VI — CONFLICTS OF INTEREST

Section 6.1. Policy. The Board adopts and annually reviews a written conflict-of-interest policy consistent with the requirements of Internal Revenue Service Form 990.

Section 6.2. Disclosure and Recusal. A director or officer who has a direct or indirect financial interest in a transaction shall disclose the interest to the Board and shall not vote on the transaction. The disinterested directors determine whether the transaction is in the corporation's best interest and is fair and reasonable, and the determination is recorded in the minutes.

ARTICLE VII — INDEMNIFICATION

Section 7.1. Indemnification. The corporation indemnifies each director and officer against liability and expenses incurred in a proceeding to which the person is a party by reason of serving in that capacity, to the fullest extent permitted by Chapter 55A of the North Carolina General Statutes.

Section 7.2. Insurance. The corporation may purchase directors and officers liability insurance.

ARTICLE VIII — PROHIBITED ACTIVITIES

Section 8.1. Private Inurement. No part of the net earnings of the corporation inures to the benefit of any director, officer, or private individual, except that the corporation may pay reasonable compensation for services rendered.

Section 8.2. Political Activity. No substantial part of the activities of the corporation is carrying on propaganda or otherwise attempting to influence legislation, and the corporation does not participate in any political campaign on behalf of or in opposition to any candidate for public office.

ARTICLE IX — DISSOLUTION

Section 9.1. Distribution on Dissolution. On dissolution, after paying or providing for its liabilities, the corporation shall distribute its remaining assets to one or more organizations described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or to a federal, state, or local government for a public purpose.

ARTICLE X — RECORDS AND FISCAL YEAR

Section 10.1. Records. The corporation keeps minutes of Board and committee proceedings, a record of its directors and officers, and appropriate accounting records at its principal office.

Section 10.2. Fiscal Year. The fiscal year ends on June 30.

ARTICLE XI — AMENDMENT

Section 11.1. Amendment. These Bylaws may be amended by a two-thirds vote of the directors then in office at any regular or special meeting, provided the substance of the proposed amendment is stated in the notice of the meeting.

CERTIFICATION

I certify that the foregoing Bylaws were adopted by the Board of Directors of Harborlight Literacy Alliance, Inc. on January 24, 2026.

/s/ Oluwaseun Adebayo-Marsh
Oluwaseun Adebayo-Marsh, Secretary
